items.info: Prince's Building, 3F 10 Chater Rd Central, Exit K. IFC Mall, Shop 3092C, Podium Level 3. · Great locally-run bookshop with a large collection on Hong Kong and China, from glossy coffee-table works to novels, local maps and hiking guides.

items.name: Dragon Culture
items.info: 231 Hollywood Rd, Sheung Wan Sheung Wan, Exit A2. 2545 8098. · Upmarket Chinese antiques, including pottery, porcelain and bronzeware; a good place to find museum-quality artefacts.

items.name: Eu Yan Sang
items.info: Shum Tower, 268 Des Voeux Rd, Central Sheung Wan, Exit A1. · Hong Kong’s most famous medicine shop, founded in 1879, and now with branches across Southeast Asia. A source of teas, herbs and Chinese medicines, all carefully weighed and measured.

items.name: Flow Bookshop
items.info: 1A Wing Cheong Commercial Building, 19-15 Jervois Street. Sheung Wan, Exit A2. · The city’s best second-hand bookshop, full of everything from holiday pulp to coffee-table albums and DVDs. Takes time to sort through the crowded shelves.

items.name: Goods of Desire
items.info: D’Aguilar Street, Central Central, Exit D2. god.com.hk . · Brilliantly eccentric store that specialises in Hong Kong-themed homewares and gifts, as well as east-meets-west fashion designs. There are several stores dotted throughout Hong Kong.

items.name: Karin Weber Gallery
items.info: 20 Aberdeen St, Central Sheung Wan, Exit A2. karinwebergallery.com . · Large selection of mid-price contemporary fine art and regular pieces of antique furniture; they also organize furniture-buying trips to warehouses on the mainland.

items.name: Linva Tailor
items.info: 38 Cochrane St, Central Central, Exit D2. · Well-established ladies’ tailor famous for its 1950s-style cheongsams - they provided the wardrobe for the stylish, moody Hong Kong romance film, In the Mood for Love . They work a lot with embroidery.

items.name: Lok Man Rare Books
items.info: 6 Chancery Lane. Central, Exit D1. lokmanbooks.com . · A step back in time, to an era of peaceful browsing, wooden bookshelves, and the scent of antique leather bindings. Particularly strong on travel and exploration but expect eyewatering prices.

items.name: Mountain Folkcraft
items.info: 12 Wo On Lane Central, Exit D mountainfolkcraft.com . · All kinds of Chinese folk art, including beautifully embroidered jackets from the Miao ethnic minority, but really excels in traditional, woodblock-printed nianhua , colourful good-luck pictures pasted up for the Chinese New Year.

items.name: Select 18
items.info: 18 Bridges Street Sheung Wan, Exit A2. 2549 2589. · Vintage clothing, spectacles, vinyl and melange of interesting old-time bric-a-brac (enamel thermos flasks, cine gear, typewriters, photos), mostly sourced from Hong Kong.

items.name: Shanghai Tang
items.info: Shop 105B, Pacific Place, 88 Queensway Admiralty, Exit C1. · New versions of traditional Chinese clothing - often in their trademark combination of pink, green and black silk - and they also offer a made-to-order service. It’s expensive, but the good, and regular sales are definitely worth a look.

items.name: Teresa Coleman Fine Arts
items.info: 55 Wyndham St, Soho Central, Exit D2. 2526 2450 (call for appointment). · Specialist in antique textiles, including Tibetan rugs and thangkas, Chinese silk robes and traditional embroideries.

items.name: Wattis Fine Art
items.info: 20 Hollywood Rd, Central Central, Exit D2. · An intriguing cave, full of China-related old maps, paintings and prints. Don't expect bargains - these are collector's prices - but it's a fascinating place for a browse.

items.name: Wing On
items.info: 211 Des Voeux Rd Sheung Wan, Exit A1. · Long-established Chinese department store selling standard day-to-day goods.

items.name: Yue Po Chai Antiques
items.info: 132-134 Hollywood Rd, Central Sheung Wan, Exit A2 2540 4374. · Browse through this maze of dusty pots, jars, plates and ephemera, and, among good-looking reproductions, you'll find some genuine antiques.

items.name: BEP
items.info: 88-90 Wellington St, Central, Exit D2. bep.hk . · Excellent Vietnamese food, cramped seating and unusually good service for Hong Kong. The tomato and crab soup, pho and rau cuon rolls are the dishes of choice. $$

items.name: Dot Cod Seafood Restaurant and Oyster Bar
items.info: Basement, Prince’s Building, 10 Chater Rd, Central Central, Exit K 2810 6988. · A chic, pricey place to eat fairly straightforward British-style seafood - rock oysters, fish and chips, scallops and char-grilled sardines. They do good breakfasts too. Set lunch $$$

items.name: Ebeneezer’s Kebabs and Pizzeria
items.info: 5 Lan Kwai Fong ebeneezers.com Central. Exit C. · A Hong Kong fast-food institution, with a number of outlets around town (including Hollywood Road) serving up no frills Middle Eastern and Indian dishes, Ebeneezer’s is a hungry budget travellers mecca, especially in the wee hours. $

items.name: Fung Shing (鳳城酒家)
items.info: G/F, Sea View Commercial Building, 21-24 Connaught Road West, Sheung Wan. Sheung Wan, Exit B 2815 8689. · Signed in Chinese, this friendly place serves excellent, inexpensive Shunde-style dim sum - try honey-roast pork or paper-thin sheung fan . $$

items.name: La Pampa
items.info: 32 Staunton St, Soho Central, Exit D2 2868 6959. · Blow out on the finest Argentinean steak, in upwards of 250g portions, grilled to your instructions and served with nominal quantities of vegetables. $$$$

items.name: Leaf Dessert/Yuk Yip (玉葉甜品)
items.info: 2 Elgin Street, Central. Sheung Wan, Exit E1. · Tiny hole-in-the-wall serving local-style desserts; somewhere to grab a sweet snack in passing, or to round off a light meal eaten elsewhere. Specialities include mung beans and kelp soup and tangyuan rice balls scattered with toasted sesame seeds and coconut. $

items.name: Lin Heung Tea House
items.info: 160-164 Wellington St, Sheung Wan Sheung Wan, Exit E1 2544 4556. · This popular, inexpensive dim sum restaurant relocated here from Guangzhou (in China) around 1950, and they’ve been so busy since, they haven’t had time to change the furnishings or allow their ancient staff to retire. Brusque atmosphere with plain, goo

items.name: Little Bao
items.info: 66 Staunton St, Central (next to PMQ) Central Exit D2, Sheung Wan Exit A2 little-bao.com . · Fun fast food based around chef May Chow’s reinvention of Chinese stuffed buns ( bao ), here served more like burgers. Don’t miss the truffle fries, spicy chicken drumstick or signature pork belly bao . $

items.name: Lock Cha Tea House
items.info: K.C. Lo Gallery, Hong Kong Park, Central Admiralty, Exit C1 2801 7177. · Elegant place furnished with carved Chinese screens and wooden tables, serving vegetarian dim sum and specialist Chinese teas - all brewed and served differently. Aimed at tourists rather than locals, though excellent quality. $$

items.name: Luk Yu Tea House
items.info: 24-26 Stanley St, just west of D’Aguilar St, Central Central, Exit D2 2523 5464. · A snapshot from the 1930s, with old wooden furniture and ceiling fans, this self-consciously traditional restaurant’s mainstay is dim sum . Despite local fame, the food, though good quality, barely justifies its tourist-inflated prices o

items.name: Man Wah
items.info: 25/F Hotel, 5 Connaught Rd Central, Exit A2 2825 4003. · Subtle and accomplished dim sum and southern Chinese food at connoisseurs’ prices ($800 a head and up), though the stunning harbour views outperform the menu. $$$$

items.name: The Peak Lookout
items.info: 121 Peak Rd, The Peak 2849 1000. · The stone colonial building with raked ceilings makes a nice setting for working your way through their Asian-Indian menu. Pricey, but reasonable value for brunch or alfresco night-time dining. $$$$

items.name: Pici
items.info: GF 45-55 Cadogan Street, Kennedy Town. Kennedy Town, Exit C 2699 1033. · Popular citywide-chain serving Italian fare including fresh hand-rolled pasta and Ravioli made from Atlantic codfish wrapped in spinach dough. This branch has outdoor seating. $$

items.name: Sam Tor
items.info: 30 Pottinger St, Central Central, Exit D2 2801 6352. · Originally famous for its “white cooked” goose innards (very crunchy; HK$60), many now opt for their wonton noodle soup (HK$28 a bowl). Get in before noon if you don’t want to join the huge queue. $

items.name: Tai Cheong Bakery
items.info: 35 Lyndhurst Terrace, Central Central, Exit D2 2544 3475. · You wouldn’t know it from the Chinese-only sign and basic tiled interior, but this tiny establishment was founded in 1954 and has since spawned a Hong Kong-wide chain. Best for Hong Kong-style egg tarts (not grilled like Macau’s version and flaky char siu past

items.name: Tak Kee Chiu Chou (德記潮州菜館)
items.info: 3 Belcher's Street, Kennedy Town. Kennedy Town, Exit B 2819 5568. · Popular restaurant specialising in dishes from the southern Chinese town of Chaozhou: steamed fish, roast goose, oyster omelette, crisp-skinned sausage, and stewed pork belly with preserved greens. Expect to wait for a table. $

items.name: Taste All Pate
items.info: 6-18 Hau Wo, Shop E Full Harvest Building Street, Kennedy Town Kennedy Town, Exit A 9650 8532. · A lovely little French bistro that serves casual fine dining that is reasonably priced for Hong Kong. $$

items.name: Tsim Chai Kee Noodle
items.info: 98 Wellington St, Central Central, Exit D2 2850 6471. · This place is easily located by the lunchtime queue tailing downhill. It’s definitely worth the wait, and even worth being jammed into the packed interior, for the famous wonton - jokingly known locally as “ping-pong wonton” because of their huge size. $

items.name: Tsui Wah
items.info: 17-19 Wellington St, Central Central, Exit D2 2525 6338. · Multistorey institution serving a huge array of inexpensive Cantonese fast food (dishes about $60), but the fishball noodle soup is the thing to go for, along with Hai Nam chicken or the very sweet desserts. Extremely busy at lunchtimes. $

items.name: Yung Kee
items.info: 32-40 Wellington St, Central Central, Exit D2 2522 1624. · A Hong Kong institution with a Michelin star, serving classic Cantonese food. Their roast pork and goose are superb, or try the set meals. $$$$

items.name: Captain’s Bar
items.info: Mandarin Oriental, 5 Connaught Rd Central. 2825 4006, mandarinoriental.com . 12pm-1am. · One of the smartest bar in Hong Kong, if not the world, this time-honoured hotel cocktail bar boasts leather-trim seating, classic cocktails as well as complimentary food menu ($$$).

items.name: Club Qing
items.info: 10/F, Cosmos Building, 8-11 Lan Kwai Fong, Central Central D2 clubqing.com . · Smart bar specialising in Japanese whisky (they claim to carry every available variety) plus rare Scotch - tasting sets are available. Also does a good line in French wine, craft beers and cocktails.

items.name: Dragon-i
items.info: The Centrium, 60 Wyndham St, Central Central D2 dragon-i.com.hk .

items.name: Fringe Club
items.info: 2 Lower Albert Rd Central, Exit D2 hkfringeclub.com . · The ground-floor bar of this theatre and art-gallery complex has good-value beers and live music, and there’s also a popular rooftop bar.

items.name: Globe
items.info: 45-53 Graham St, Soho Central theglobe.com.hk . · Immense bar known for one of the longest lists of local and imported beers in the city, plus craft beers and solid comfort food of the British pub grub verve ($$).

items.name: Havana Bar
items.info: 4/F, The Plaza, 21 D’Aguilar Street, Lan Kwai Fong Central, Exit D2 havanabar.com.hk . · This popular bar offers a reprieve from Lan Kwai Fong’s evening crowds, with a spacious terrace and the largest selection of rum in the city. Good tapas too ($$).

items.name: Insomnia
items.info: 38-44 D’Aguilar St, Lan Kwai Fong Central, Exit D2 2525 0957. · Street-side bar where, early in the evening, conversation is possible. Later, the house band plays covers at full volume.

items.name: Origin
items.info: G/F, 48 Wyndham St Central, Exit D2 2668 5583. · Brick and exposed dark timber interior lend tropical ambiance to what is, essentially, a very stylish gin bar, serving Mother’s Ruin in a bewildering variety of cocktails.

items.name: Peel Fresco Music Lounge
items.info: 49 Peel St, Central Sheung Wan Exit E1 peel-fresco.com . · Slightly outrageously claims to be Hong Kong’s only true live music venue - though fair enough if you’re looking for a dark, atmospheric, crowded jazz club. Hosts regular local talent, plus visiting bands.

items.name: Quench K-Town
items.info: 1H Sands Street, Kennedy Town Kennedy Town Exit B 2321 9291. · Classic sports bar serving pub grub ($$) and pints of beer to a predominantly expat crowd. Can get packed during big sporting events.

items.name: Volar
items.info: Basement 38-44 D’Aguillar St, Lan Kwai Fong Central Exit D2 facebook.com/volarhongkong . · Long-established, chic dance club known for its star DJs and over-the-top sound system belting out r’n’b, hip-hop and electronica.

items.name: The Convention and Exhibition Centre
items.info: Convention Avenue Wan Chai, Exit A1 hkcec.com . · The standout Convention and Exhibition Centre , whose distinctively flattened, curved roof juts out into the harbour, is where the British formally handed Hong Kong back to China in June 1997. As such, it’s a huge draw with Chinese tourists, who come to pose beside the

items.name: Central Plaza
items.info: Harbour Rd Wan Chai, Exit A1. · Sited opposite the Convention and Exhibition Centre, Central Plaza is another notable architectural marvel - it’s the world’s tallest building made of reinforced concrete (374m). Triangular in shape, it’s topped by a glass pyramid from which a 64m mast protrudes: the locals dubbed it “Th

items.name: Queen’s Road East
items.info: Admiralty, Exit J. · Inland, up against The Peak’s foothills, Queen’s Road East features a concentration of furniture stores, many offering fine-quality reproduction antique Chinese wooden chairs, screens and tables. Around halfway down, Hung Shing Temple occupies a natural grotto right on the roadside and is dedicated

items.name: Bowen Road and Lovers Rock
items.info: Wan Chai. · It’s a stiff hike up lanes from beside the Old Wan Chai Post Office or Pak Tai Temple to Bowen Road , a level pedestrian path among the thick forest above Wan Chai, offering occasional glimpses of the city through the canopy. It’s a popular spot with walkers and joggers, and is amazingly wild given its loca

items.name: The Noon Day Gun
items.info: Gloucester Rd Causeway Bay, Exit D1. · Ever since colonial times, a ship’s cannon known as the Noon Day Gun has been fired daily across the harbour at Wan Chai. Nobody seems to know why - there are several conflicting stories - and with mainland Chinese influence growing in Hong Kong, there’s talk of the ceremony being

items.name: Victoria Park
items.info: Causeway Bay, Exit E. 24hr. · Sited east of Gloucester Road, Victoria Park is a flat, spacious spread of paving, sports fields and ornamental borders. It’s busy around the clock, with martial arts practitioners and old men airing their caged songbirds at the crack of dawn, people cooling off on benches under the trees

items.name: Times Square
items.info: Causeway Bay, Exit A timessquare.com.hk . · The most startling fixture in the Causeway Bay shopping area is the beige blockbuster of a building that is Times Square , at the corner of Matheson and Russell streets. Spearing skywards, it exemplifies Hong Kong’s modern architecture, where only vertical space is available

items.name: Happy Valley Racecourse
items.info: Causeway Bay hkjc.com . · Once a malarial swamp, initially settled, then abandoned, by the British, Happy Valley - or pau ma dei (horseracing track) in Cantonese - means one thing only to locals: gambling. All other forms of betting are banned in Hong Kong, and the Happy Valley Racecourse is the traditional centre of t

items.name: The Cemeteries
items.info: Wong Nai Chung Rd Causeway Bay. Free. · The series of terraced hillside cemeteries west of the racecourse provides an interesting snapshot of the territory’s ethnic and religious mix during its earliest days, with separate enclosures for Muslim, Catholic, Protestant, Parsee and Jewish inhabitants. The large Protestant

items.name: Museum of Coastal Defence
items.info: POCKET MAP L5 Shau Kei Wan/tram or bus #2 from Central to Shau Kei Wan, then a signed 1km walk along Shau Kei Wan Main St. hk.coastaldefence.museum . · Actually some way east from Causeway Bay, the Museum of Coastal Defence occupies the site of the Lei Yue Mun Fort, built by the British in 1887 to defend Victoria Harbo

items.name: 298 Computer Zone
items.info: 298 Hennessy Rd, Wan Chai Wan Chai, Exit A4. · Despite the massive sign outside, it’s hard to find the entrance to this warren-like place, a shopping arcade and emporium selling smart-phone, gaming and computer gear on three levels. Reasonably priced accessories and software available to those willing to walk and talk.

items.name: Just Gold
items.info: SOGO, Hennessy Rd, Wan Chai Causeway Bay, Exit D. 2891 1643. · Local chain specialising in fun, fashionable, well-priced jewellery designs for young women.

items.name: Kee Wah Bakery (奇華餠家)
items.info: 188 Queen's Road East Wan Chai Exit A5 keewah.com . · Founded in 1936, and housed inside a period-style building at the end of Lee Tung Avenue, this place is renowned for its traditional Cantonese mooncakes and pineapple buns.

items.name: Ki Chan Tea Co.
items.info: 174 Johnston Rd, Wan Chai Wan Chai, Exit A3 kichantea.com . · Polished wooden counters and tea leaves stored in metal cylinders set the scene in this traditional, long-established shop.

items.name: Lane Crawford
items.info: Shop 126, Pacific Place 2, 88 Queensway, Wan Chai Admiralty, Exit C1. · Hong Kong’s oldest Western-style department store, with a well-stocked inventory of smart - if sometimes stuffy - designer brands from around the globe.

items.name: Lee Gardens
items.info: Yun Ping Rd, Causeway Bay Causeway Bay, Exit F. · Two huge towers housing upmarket shopping malls and a selection of good restaurants.

items.name: Sogo
items.info: 555 Hennessy Rd, Causeway Bay Causeway Bay, Exit D. · Hong Kong’s first Japanese department store, and the largest of its kind in the SAR, this enormous complex covers thirteen floors and seems to sell just about everything.

items.name: Times Square
items.info: Russell St, Causeway Bay Causeway Bay, Exit A. · An iconic structure, containing over two hundred shops on sixteen floors, featuring all of Hong Kong’s major brands, plus plenty of international ones as well.

items.name: Vivienne Tam
items.info: Shop 428, 1 Matheson St, Causeway Bay Causeway Bay, Exit A viviennetam.com . · Funky shirts and dresses in David Hockney-meets-Vivienne Westwood style, often featuring Chairman Mao and other icons of the East. Pricey.

items.name: Bowrington Road Market
items.info: Bowrington Rd, Wan Chai Causeway Bay, Exit A. Daily 24hr. · A full-on, bustling Chinese produce market wedged in between busy roads and flyovers, with a cooked food area upstairs selling inexpensive one-dish meals and noodle soups. $

items.name: Cinta-J
items.info: G/F, Malaysia Building, 69 Jaffe Rd, Wan Chai Wan Chai, Exit A1 2529 6622. · Legendary Indonesian and Filipino restaurant-bar, with a fantastic live band after dark most nights. Mains around $70; their sweet chilli squid and sour fish soup are the genuine article. $$

items.name: Crystal Jade
items.info: Basement 2, Times Square, Causeway Bay Causeway Bay, Exit A 2506 0080. · Popular branch of a city-wide Shanghainese snack chain, serving excellent xiaolongbao - steamed pork dumplings in a thin, wheat-dough wrapper - and spicy noodle soups. $

items.name: Drunken Jade Restaurant (Chui King Lau)
items.info: 289 Hennessy Rd, Causeway Bay Wan Chai, Exit A2 2511 1848. · Don't be put off by the lack of English signage (look for 醉瓊樓酒家); this small restaurant serves great Hakka-style dim sum and one-pot set meals. $$

items.name: Fook Lam Moon
items.info: 35-45 Johnston Rd, Wan Chai Wan Chai, Exit B 2866 0663. · Among Hong Kong’s most famous Cantonese restaurants. House specialities include bird’s nest in coconut milk, abalone, crispy piglet and crisp-skinned chicken. $$$$

items.name: Hay! (喜遇)
items.info: G01, Lee Tung Ave Wan Chai Exit A3 welovehay.com . · Shanghai snacks - drunken chicken, four-treasures kaofu, egg white and broadbeans, xiaolongbao - served in a bright, informal, busy environment. $$

items.name: Hee Kee
items.info: 379 Jaffe Rd, Wan Chai Causeway Bay, Exit C. · Minimalist location for consuming deep-fried whole crab with chillies ($600), said to be an old Causeway Bay speciality. Sporadically popular with Hong Kong film stars. $$$$

items.name: Kung Tak Lam
items.info: 10/F, World Trade Centre, Causeway Bay Causeway Bay, Exit E 2881 9966. · Shanghai-style vegetarian restaurant specializing in “meat” dishes, though the food - while tasty enough - is nowhere near as good as the view out over the harbour. $$

items.name: Lei Garden
items.info: 1/F, CNT Tower, 338 Hennessy Road, Wan Chai Wan Chai Exit A3. 2892 0333. · Long-running chain with a very good standard of Chaozhou-style dim sum , including crispy-skinned pork, cheung fan stuffed rice rolls, fried turnip cake and transparent fun gwor . $$

items.name: Metropol
items.info: 4/F, United Centre, 95 Queensway, Wan Chai Admiralty, Exit D 2865 1988. · Huge dim sum hall, very child-friendly, with views of Convention Centre. Try the flaky char siu pastries and crunchy prawn dumplings, served from trollies. $$

items.name: Mother of Pizzas
items.info: 13/19 Leighton Rd Causeway Bay, Exit 1 2891 2221. · As its name suggests, this place serves some seriously hearty Italian fare. Still, if you don’t fear the carbs this a great venue to unwind in after a hard day’s shopping, located a few blocks beyond the hubbub of Causeway Bay. Pizza is served by the slice for takeawa

items.name: The Optimist
items.info: 239 Hennessy Rd, Wan Chai Wan Chai, Exit A2 2433 3324. · Set over three floors, this fancy-looking place seeks to bring a bit of “Barcelona chic” to Hong Kong with fine Mediterranean fare including Northern Spanish tapas. The drinks list includes craft beers, wines, cocktails and daily Happy Hour every day from 3pm unt

items.name: Plaza Mayor
items.info: 4 Sun St, Wan Chai Wan Chai, Exit B1 or B2 plazamayor.hk . · Tiny place with black-and-white tiling, a marble counter, excellent tapas - try the iberico ham and garlic shrimps - and good Spanish wine. $$$

items.name: Shuangxi Lou (雙喜樓)
items.info: Shop G32, Lee Tung Ave Wan Chai Exit A3 2805 8828. · Bright, modern restaurant serving traditional Cantonese dim sum - go for the steamed spare ribs, crispy-skinned pork and meltingly soft char siu pork. $$

items.name: Wing Wah (永華麵家)
items.info: 89 Hennessy Rd, Wan Chai Wan Chai, Exit B 2527 7476. · Locally famous for its wonton noodle soup ($34), which is what they’ll bring you by default unless you ask for something else - such as their sweet red bean and tangerine peel soup. $

items.name: Yu (渝酸辣粉)
items.info: 4 Yiu Wa St, Causeway Bay, Exit A 2838 8198. · A fine little restaurant serving delicious Sichuan style fare, including rice noodles and spicy chicken as well as some cold and vegetarian dishes. $$

items.name: Carnegie’s
items.info: 53-55 Lockhart Rd, Wan Chai Wan Chai, Exit C 2866 6289. · The noise level here means conversation is only possible by flash cards; once it’s packed, hordes of punters keen to revel the night away fight for dancing space on the bar. Hosts the occasional riotous club night and regular live music.

items.name: Devil's Advocate
items.info: 48-50 Lockhart Rd, Wan Chai Wan Chai, Exit C 2865 7271. · Long-running, raucously popular sports' bar which attracts a younger crowd. If you can cope with the terrible 1970s soundtrack, come along during the happy hour for excellent deals or on Wednesdays for further discounts.

items.name: Dusk Till Dawn
items.info: 76 Jaffe Rd, Wan Chai Wan Chai, Exit C 2528 4689. · Vaguely Mediterranean colours decorate this rowdy bar, full of loud live music, raucous staff and hoarse punters.

items.name: Executive Bar
items.info: 27 Floor Bartlock Centre, 3 Yiu Wa Street, Wan Chai Causeway Bay, Exit A 2893 2080. · A quiet, classy hideaway up on the 27th floor serving whiskies from Scotland, Ireland, Japan and the US to be enjoyed over a picture-postcard view of Happy Valley Racecourse below.

items.name: Joe Banana’s
items.info: 23 Luard Rd Wan Chai, Exit C joebananas.hk . · Iconic British-style bar that has been in business for decades, with a late disco, fake palms and regular live music. You need to be (or look) 21 to get in and there’s a strict door policy - men need a shirt with a collar. Also does lunch and coffee by day ($$).

items.name: TED’s Lookout
items.info: G/F, Moonful Court, 17A Moon St, Wan Chai Wan Chai, Exit B2 2520 0076. · Cute - or just plain small - restaurant-bar in a quiet cul-de-sac; the Tex-Mex style food ($$) is above average, but the drinks are superb, if pricey.

items.name: The Wanch
items.info: 1/F, 90 Jeffe Rd thewanch.hk Wan Chai. · Having closed in 2020 due to the Covid-19 pandemic, Hong Kong’s first boozy rock dive reopened in 2022. Live gigs, pub grub (including cheap burgers and sandwiches; $$) and affordable drinks (for Hong Kong) is the recipe for a good night out.

items.name: Aberdeen
items.info: Bus #7 from Outer Islands Ferry Pier, Central; #70 from Exchange Square, Central; or #72 from Moreton Terrace, Causeway Bay. · Aberdeen was already settled when the British arrived in the 1840s - the bay here was used by the Indigenous Hoklos and Tankas, who fished in the surrounding archipelago. The harbour remains Ab

items.name: Ocean Park
items.info: Bus #629 from Central Ferry Piers oceanpark.com.hk . $468, under-11s $249; includes all rides and entry. · Filling a whole peninsula, Ocean Park is an open-air theme park and oceanarium; it also features four giant pandas , for whom a special two-thousand-square-metre complex has been created.

items.name: Repulse Bay
items.info: Bus #6, #6A, #61, #64 or #260 from Exchange Square, Central. · Increasingly built up with tower blocks, Repulse Bay is named after the British warship HMS Repulse , which mopped up local pirates in the nineteenth century and later the area was known for the cocktail parties held at the grand Repulse Bay Hotel . The hot

items.name: Stanley
items.info: Bus #6, #6A or #260 from Exchange Square, Central. · When Britain seized Hong Kong there were already two thousand people living at the south coast settlement of Stanley , earning an income from fishing and piracy. Today, it’s a small residential place, with low-key modern buildings and number of good pubs and restaura

items.name: The Dragon’s Back
items.info: Bus #9 from Shau Kei Wan (next to the MTR station) or Shek O. · The Dragon’s Back is the final section of the 50km-long Hong Kong Island Trail , which runs west to east across the island. Though the name sounds fierce, the two-hour hike is not too difficult, and at weekends you’re likely to find plenty of other people

items.name: Shek O
items.info: Bus #9 from Shau Kei Wan (next to the MTR station); or Sun only bus #309 from Exchange Square, Central. · Shek O is an unpretentious village down at Hong Kong’s southeastern reaches, with the best beach on the island. Wide, with white sand and fringed by shady trees, it can get very full at the weekend. There are also

items.name: Aberdeen Fisherman’s Wharf
items.info: 2a Reclamation Area House boat, Tin Kwong, Pier 6, Aberdeen. Call first fishermanswharf.hk . · Established in 2022 in an old fisherman’s boat, this souvenir store showcases locally crafted goods and edible products including artworks, literature and seafood products. It also houses a tourist info desk.

items.name: Horizon Plaza
items.info: 2 Lee Wing St, Ap Lei Chau island. South Horizons, Exit C horizonplazahk.com . · 25 storeys of discount furnishings and designer fashion labels - Hong Kong’s major upmarket clothing stores, such as Joyce Boutique (21/F), send all last season’s stock here. Also try the Old Shanghai (15/F) and Oriental Chest (12/F).

items.name: L&E Arts and Crafts
items.info: 11A Kwai Bo Industrial Building, 40 Wong Chuk Hang Rd, Aberdeen, Call first lneco.com · Stalwart of antique - and antique-style - home furnishings; a great place for a browse.

items.name: Happy Garden
items.info: Near the bus stop, Shek O 2809 4165. · One of several laidback places with outdoor tables, luridly coloured drinks and excellent food - try the water spinach with belechan beef, or huge Thai fish cakes. $$

items.name: King Ludwig Beerhall
items.info: 2nd Floor. Murray House, Stanley 2899 0122. · This Bavarian restaurant and bar is actually housed in Murray House offering diners incredible views of Stanley harbour. Look out for the weekend brunch buffet. $$

items.name: Paramount Banquet Hall

items.name: Lung Wah

Still, the run-down palatial splendour and strutting caged peacocks are worth a look, even if you choose not to dine. $$

items.name: Tao Heung
items.info: Shop A, Fuller Garden, 8 Chui Lok Street, Tai Po 2666 9923. · Main dishes are fairly ordinary, but a great place for dim sum : try the white radish cake, roast pork cheung fan (stuffed rice noodles) and the beef rissoles with celery. $$$

items.name: Tung Kee Seafood
items.info: Waterfront, Sai Kung Town 2792 7453. · This is a cheerful, noisy (and slightly overpriced) place, whose speciality is “bamboo fish”: carp, stuffed with preserved turnip, and chargrilled outside on a hand-rotated bamboo pole. $$

items.name: Hong Kong Disneyland
items.info: Disneyland hongkongdisneyland.com . Charge. · The world’s smallest Disneyland , this theme park is worth a visit if you’ve time to kill between flights, but it’s a bit tame compared with Disney’s ten other franchises, and queues can also be a drag.

items.name: Tung Chung and Ngong Ping 360
items.info: Tung Chung np360.com.hk . Charge; reduced fee for children. · Tung Chung is a burgeoning New Town and transport hub close to Hong Kong’s International Airport on Lantau’s north coast. Its main attraction is the 5.7km, 25-minute-long Ngong Ping 360 cable car ride up the mountainside to Po Lin Monastery and the Big Buddh

items.name: Lantau Peak
items.info: The 934m Lantau Peak , more properly known as Fung Wong Shan, is the second highest in Hong Kong, and a popular place to watch the sun rise - you can stay the night before at the S.G. Davis Youth Hostel . The steep 2km trail from Po Lin to the summit takes about an hour to complete, and on a clear day views reach as fa

items.name: Po Lin Monastery and the Tian Tan Big Buddha
items.info: Ngong Ping. Bus #2 from Mui Wo, #21 from Tai O or #23 from Tung Chung; or cable car from Tung Chung. Monastery. · Hidden behind an ornamental stone archway, the Po Lin Monastery was founded in 1906 and has grown to be the largest Chan (Zen) Buddhist temple in Hong Kong. The front hall sports dynamic carvings of phoenix

items.name: Tai O
items.info: Bus #1 from Mui Wo, #11 from Tung Chung or #21 from Po Lin Monastery. · The largest and oldest village on Lantau, Tai O is an atmospheric jumble of lanes, shrines and temples, and features a quarter full of tin-roofed stilt-houses built over the water, home to two thousand people. From the bus stop, you cross a small b

items.name: The south coast
items.info: Lantau’s best beaches line the south coast . All of them are accessible on foot from Mui Wo along the Lantau Trail, or by bus #1 or #2 (to Tai O and Po Lin Monastery respectively from Mui Wo) as far as Shek Pik Reservoir. Closest to Mui Wo is Pui O beach (9km; 3hr on foot), an excellent spot with barbecue pits and a fr

items.name: Mui Wo and around
items.info: Mui Wo , also known as Silvermine Bay, is a small residential community surrounding Lantau’s ferry port, with a beach, several hiking trails, some pleasant accommodation and restaurants and a major bus terminus. Mui Wo marks the eastern end of the Lantau Trail , and also the 5.7km Olympic Trail to Tung Chung, which pas

items.name: Lamma
items.info: Lamma is an elongated fourteen-square-kilometre stretch of land inhabited by five thousand people, with well-marked paths linking its settlements to small beaches, green hilltops and pleasant seascapes. Yung Shue Wan is a pretty, tree-shaded village at the northwestern end of the island, where the bulk of Lamma’s resid

items.name: Cheung Chau
items.info: Cheung Chau (“Long Island”) was the stronghold of the Qing dynasty pirate Cheung Po Tsai. Along with his forty thousand followers, he terrorized shipping and villages along the adjacent Chinese coast, reputedly hiding his booty in a cave at Cheung Chau’s southern end. After surrendering to government forces in 1810, he

items.name: Concerto Inn
items.info: Hung Shing Ye beach, Lamma concertoinn.com.hk . · Near a small and quiet beach, this hotel-restaurant is set on a delightful terrace and serves an eclectic range of Asian and Western dishes. $$

items.name: Jaybird Restaurant
items.info: Yung Shue Wan, opposite the ferry pier 6026 3693. · Popular and friendly Western-style café with outdoor seating and harbour views. Mains around $60. Plenty of vegetarian options. $

items.name: Lamma Seaview Man Fung Restaurant
items.info: Near the pier, Yung Shue Wan, Lamma 2982 0719. · Fresh and flavourful crab, abalone, fish from live tanks and a long list of budget rice and noodle dishes are on the menu here, served at outdoor waterfront tables under beach umbrellas, offering pleasant views while you enjoy your meal. $$$

items.name: Rainbow Seafood
items.info: 23-25 First Street, Sok Kwu Wan, Lamma rainbowrest.com.hk . · At this place you’re invited to pick your fresh seafood directly from the tank. Along with lightly steamed whole fish, there’s masterful deep-fried squid with chillies and salt. Slightly overpriced, with set menus for two. $$$

items.name: Largo do Senado
items.info: Largo do Senado (Senate Square) is Macau’s public focus, cobbled and surrounded by elegant colonial buildings painted pale pink, yellow or white, with shuttered upper storeys and street-level colonnades. Leal Senado , the Senate House itself (free), faces Largo do Senado on Avenida de Almeida Ribeiro. It’s of tradition

items.name: São Paulo
items.info: North of São Domingos, through a nest of cobbled lanes flanked by pastelarias (shops selling sweets, biscuits and roast meats), stands the imposing facade of São Paulo church. Founded in 1602, its rich design reflected the cosmopolitan nature of early Macau - designed by an Italian in a Spanish style, and built by Japa

items.name: Fortaleza do Monte
items.info: 22 Calcada das Verdades. Free. · East of São Paulo the solid Fortaleza do Monte , once part of the São Paulo complex, saw action only once, when its cannons helped repel the Dutch in 1622. The ramparts, lined with the weathered cannons, give views over almost the whole peninsula.

items.name: Hong Kung Temple
items.info: Rua Cinco de Outubro. · The unpretentious Hong Kung Temple is dedicated to Kwan Tai, god of riches and war, and is the focus for the extraordinary Drunken Dragon Festival , held on the eighth day of the fourth lunar month (April or May). Organized by the Fish Retailers’ Association, the festival features opera, religio

items.name: Jardim Luís de Camōes
items.info: Praça Luís de Camões. Free. · The Jardim Luís de Camões (Camões Garden) is a very tropical, laidback spread of banyans, ferns, fan palms, paved terraces and flowers. It’s always full of people pottering about, exercising or playing cards under the trees, and commemorates the sixteenth-century Portuguese poet who is sup

items.name: Cemitério Protestante
items.info: Rua de Entre Campos. Free. · The Cemitério Protestante (Old Protestant Cemetery) houses many of the non-Portuguese traders and visitors who expired in the enclave. For decades, Protestants had no set burial place in Macau: the Catholic Portuguese didn’t want them and the Chinese objected if they were interred on ancest

items.name: Jardim Lou Lim Ioc
items.info: Av. do Conselheiro Ferreira de Almeida. Free. · A high wall encloses the beautiful Jardim Lou Lim Ioc , a formal arrangement of pavilions, carp ponds, bamboo groves and frangipani trees. Built in the nineteenth century by the wealthy Chinese merchant Lou Kou, it was modelled on the famous classical Chinese gardens of S

items.name: Guia Hill
items.info: Av. Sidónio Pais. · Guia Hill , Macau’s apex and site of its former defence headquarters, is now a landscaped park. Paths wind to the top from the entrances on Estrada da Vittoria and Avenida Sidónio Pais; from the latter, there’s also a cable car link to the top (charge). Either way, you’ll end up a short walk from th

items.name: Kun Iam Temple
items.info: Av. do Coronel Mesquita. Free. · Entered through a banyan-planted courtyard crowded with fortune-tellers, the scruffy, 400-year-old Kun Iam Temple is dedicated to the Bodhisattva of mercy (known in Hong Kong as Kwun Yam), and was the venue for the signing of the first ever Sino-American treaty on July 3, 1844 by Vicero

items.name: Lin Kai Temple and around
items.info: Travessa da Corda, off Estrada do Repouso. Free. · Tucked down a side lane off main Estrada do Repouso, Lin Kai Temple is a maze of small halls dedicated to a host of local deities, including the Fire God, Ua Kwong, whose festival is held on the 28th day of the ninth lunar month (some point in Oct). The temple is old,

items.name: Three Lamps District and the Red Market
items.info: Rotunda de Carlos da Maia. · A few minutes’ walk from the Lin Kai Temple, a roundabout marks the centre of the pedestrianized Sam Jan Dang or Three Lamps District . The streets immediately north of here are packed with busy market stalls selling bedding, fabrics, fresh produce and - especially - clothes ; bargain hard

items.name: The Lin Fong Temple and Museu Lin Zexu
items.info: Av. do Almirante Lacerda. · About 500m north of the Red Market, the Lin Fong Temple (free) was established in 1592 to provide accommodation for travelling officials. It’s full of gaudy woodwork painted gold and red, coloured wall mouldings of fantastic beasts and very fine stone carvings above the entrances depicting m

items.name: The border
items.info: Bus #5 from the Lin Fong Temple runs a kilometre north to the border with China , past an escalation of shops and backstreet markets selling all the things you might have forgotten to buy - or never even realized were for sale - during your stay. Many of the people here are mainland Chinese, buying powdered milk in bul

items.name: Rua da Felicidade
items.info: On the west side of the southern peninsula is the Porto Interior or Inner Harbour, formerly Macau’s main port area. Between here and the Leal Senado is a warren of backstreets. The most interesting is Rua da Felicidade (Happiness Street). This was once a red-light district but now - even though there are sex workers- i

items.name: The Barra
items.info: The Barra is the district at the southern end of Macau’s peninsula, cut by Rua Central and its continuations, a dense collection of nineteenth-century civic buildings and cheap Chinese cafés, clothes-making workshops and small businesses. On Rua Central, the peppermint-coloured Teatro Dom Pedro V (free) dates to 1873;

items.name: A-Ma Temple
items.info: Rua do Almirante Sérgio. Free. · The A-Ma Temple is Macau’s oldest place of worship, founded in 1370 and named after a girl whose spirit would appear to save people at sea (known in Hong Kong as Tin Hau and elsewhere in Southeast Asia as Mazu). When the Portuguese made their first landfall here in the early 1550s, they

items.name: Museu Marítimo
items.info: Rua do Almirante Sérgio. marine.gov.mo . Free. · Macau’s Museu Marítimo (Maritime Museum; free) is an engaging and well-presented collection relating to local fishing techniques and festivals, Chinese and Portuguese maritime prowess, and boat-building. There’s navigational equipment, a scale model of seventeenth-centur

items.name: Fortaleza de São Tiago da Barra
items.info: Pousada de São Tiago, Rua São Tiago da Barra. · Set at Macau’s southernmost tip, the Fortaleza da Barra was once Macau’s most important fortress. Completed in 1629, it was designed with 10m-high walls and lined with cannons to protect the entrance to the Inner Harbour, then just offshore (though land reclamation has co

items.name: Avenida da Amizade and the Porto Exterior
items.info: The modern area southeast of Guia Hill is built on land reclaimed from the Porto Exterior (Outer Harbour) over the last few decades. The main artery here is the multi-laned Avenida da Amizade , whose southern end is marked by the orange-tiled Lisboa . It’s Macau’s most famous hotel and a roaring, 1930s-style casino, cr

items.name: Taipa Village
items.info: Taipa’s main point of interest is old Taipa Village , a few narrow streets surrounding a couple of faded old squares. The Portuguese and Macanese restaurants here are one attraction, and on Sundays (noon-9pm) the streets are packed with a handicraft market. Rua do Cunha is the main street, a narrow pedestrianized lane

items.name: Cotai and the Venetian
items.info: The recently created land connecting Taipa with Coloane is known as Cotai , an up-and-coming entertainment district featuring yet more casinos, including the Venetian , a full-scale reproduction of Venice’s St Mark’s Square. This houses the world’s largest casino resort, with 850 gaming tables, 4100 slot machines and i

items.name: Coloane
items.info: Coloane was once a base for pirates who hid out in its cliffs and caves, seizing the cargoes of trading ships passing between Macau and China. Today, the island’s main draws are its peaceful surroundings, beaches and a village with the usual mix of temples and colonial leftovers.

items.name: 360º Café
items.info: Level 60, Macau Tower 8988 8623, macautower.com.mo . · Smart revolving restaurant with unparalleled city views, serving Indian, Macanese and plain grilled seafood. One way not to bankrupt yourself is to opt for the set lunch buffets or afternoon tea from 3.30pm. $$$

items.name: A Lorcha
items.info: Rua do Almirante Sérgio 298 2831 3193, alorcha.com . · This wood-beamed restaurant serves outstanding Portuguese food and is always busy. There’s a large menu of staples, including serradura , a spectacular cream and biscuit dessert. $$$

items.name: A Petisqueira
items.info: 15 Rua de S. João, Taipa Village 2882 5354. · With its relaxing green interior, this friendly, well-regarded Portuguese restaurant has all the usual favourites including delicious home-style paella. $$

items.name: Boa Mesa
items.info: Travessa do S. Domingos 16A, between the Sé and Largo do Senado 2838 9453. · A relaxed, friendly place taking pride in its farm-bred pig dishes and sumptuous chocolate mousse. Set meals start around MOP$110, and even a la carte it’s not too expensive. $$

items.name: Café Nga Tim/Chan Chi Mei
items.info: Largo Eduardo Marques, in front of the Xavier Chapel, Coloane Village 2888 2086. · Inexpensive menu of Chinese, Macanese and Portuguese dishes, excelling in fresh seafood. $$

items.name: Cathedral Café
items.info: 12 R. da Sé 12 6685 7621. · Just a few blocks from Senado Square, this is a great place to grab a Lusophone breakfast, lunch or dinner, as well as a good glass of wine or an evening cocktail. $$

items.name: Clube Militar
items.info: Av. da Praia Grande 975 2871 4010. · This private club in the São Francisco barracks has an elegant colonial dining room open to the public. The a la carte Portuguese menu is dear, but the set-price lunch buffet is fantastic value (around MOP$150 a head). There’s also a ‘no sportswear’ dress code. $$$

items.name: Fat Siu Lau
items.info: Rua da Felicidade 64 9857 3580, fatsiulau.com.mo . · One of Macau’s oldest and most famous Chinese restaurants. Pigeon is the house speciality, but otherwise their African chicken (MOP$180) is also good. $$

items.name: Fernando
items.info: Hác Sá Beach, Coloane 2888 2264. · The good Portuguese food and a casual, beach-side atmosphere make this long-running place a favourite with expats. Book in advance and be prepared to catch a taxi home. $$

items.name: Galo
items.info: Calçado do Tronco Velho 10 2882 7318, galomacau.com . · Decorated in Portuguese country chic, with a menu sporting boiled meats, steaks, grilled squid or crab, and large mixed salads. Not fine cuisine, but hearty and full of flavour. $$

items.name: Litoral
items.info: Rua do Almirante Sérgio 261 2896 7878. · Rated by some as serving the best Portuguese and Macanese food in Macau, with a menu based on old family recipes including curried crab and stewed pork with shrimp paste. $$$

items.name: Lord Stow’s Bakery
items.info: Coloane Village Square, Coloane. · Although British-owned, this is one of the best places to eat natas (baked custard tarts), made from a secret improved recipe without animal fat. Buy takeaways from the bakery or have coffee and a light meal at their café around the corner. $$

items.name: Mariazinha
items.info: Rua do Monte 8 2835 7558. · Excellent Portuguese restaurant, offering everything from a roast pork sandwich to a three-course blow-out of Iberian ham, cod and almond cake. They know their wines, too. $$$

items.name: Nam Ping
items.info: Rua de Cinco de Outubro 85 2892 2267. · Old-time Macanese café, serving home-baked sugared doughnuts, custard tarts, and ham and egg sandwiches. $

items.name: O Santos
items.info: Rua da Cunha, Taipa Village 2822 7508. · Hearty, home-style Portuguese food, delivered with little ceremony but in healthy portions: seafood, pork and bean stew, rabbit and roast suckling pig. $$

items.name: Riquexó
items.info: Av. de Sidónio Pais 69-B 2856 5655. · Basic Portuguese canteen, with little atmosphere and a limited menu but popular for its low prices. Go for the feijoada or curry chicken. $

items.name: Lan Fong Yuen
items.info: This classic cha chaan tang (tea house) is the originator of Hong Kong-style milk tea. 7.30am-6pm Mon-Sat $$

items.name: Yat Lok
items.info: Known for its delicious roast goose and brusque service. Go at 3.30pm to 4pm to beat the queues. 10am-8.30pm Thu-Tue $$

items.name: Ser Wong Fun
items.info: Dishes are designed for groups, but you can pop in for a single serving of the famous ‘five-snake soup’. 11am-9.30pm $$

items.name: Tai Cheong Bakery
items.info: Hymn to Old Hong Kong · Long celebrated for its egg tarts, and a favourite of Hong Kong’s last governor Chris Patten. 9.30am-7.30pm $

items.name: Tsim Chai Kee Noodle
items.info: Cheap, cheerful noodle specialist serving al dente noodles with plump fish balls in a light, seafood broth. 11am-9.30pm $

items.name: Sing Kee
items.info: One of Central’s few remaining dai pai dong (open-air food stalls), this Stanley Street spot is known for its cheap seafood dishes. 11am-3pm, 6-11pm Mon-Sat $

items.name: Samdor Noodle
items.info: Tiny Samdor is a legit noodle specialist serving wonton soup packed with prawn-and-pork parcels and toothsome noodles. $

items.name: Wang Fu
items.info: Skyscraper Spotting Safari · Take a break from dim sum and try the jiǎozi (northern Chinese boiled dumplings) at this humble spot. 11am-10pm Sun-Fri $

items.name: Luk Yu Tea House
items.info: Once the haunt of opera artists, writers and painters, this grand tea house (c 1933) serves dim sum and Cantonese dishes. 7am-10pm $$

items.name: City Hall Maxim’s Palace
items.info: Dim sum is served on carts in a packed, noisy dining hall emblazoned with dragons. 11am-3pm, 5.30-11pm Mon-Sat, from 9am Sun $$

items.name: One Dim Sum
items.info: Grab super dim sum at this fast-casual joint just off the Central-Mid-Levels Escalator. 10am-9pm Mon-Thu, to midnight Fri, 8am-midnight Sat, 8am-8pm Sun $

items.name: Ding Dim 1968
items.info: Little Manilla in Central · Reliably tasty dim sum near Lan Kwai Fong. Try the xiǎolóngbāo (steamed buns) filled with ‘secret’ soup. 11am-10pm Sun-Thu, to 11pm Fri & Sat $

items.name: Mott 32
items.info: Known for its applewood-roasted Peking duck (pre-order only), and named after the address of New York’s first Chinese grocery shop. $$$

items.name: Duddell’s
items.info: Exquisite renditions of Cantonese favourites. All-you-can-eat weekend brunches can be paired with free-flowing champagne. noon-3pm & 6-11pm Mon-Sat $$$

items.name: Madame Fu Grand Cafe Chinois
items.info: Inside Tai Kwun; creative Cantonese fare like steamed egg-custard with lobster and caviar. 11am-midnight Mon-Fri, to 12.30am Sat & Sun $$$

items.name: Ho Lee Fook
items.info: Drop Anchor at Central Harbourfront Set Sail into History · Buzzy underground spot doing a fun fusion take on Chinese and Cantonese fare, served to the sounds of old-school jams and 1980s Canto-pop. 6-10.30pm $$

items.name: New Punjab Club
items.info: The world’s first Michelin-starred Pakistani restaurant; spicy sharing dishes and contemporary Pakistani art. noon-2.30pm & 6-10.30pm $$$

items.name: Obp
items.info: An uber-cool Korean ‘speakeasy’ for those in the know, with lip-smacking fried chicken, seafood pancakes and post-drinks party vibes. 5.30pm-midnight $$

items.name: Chom Chom
items.info: Contemporary Vietnamese in cool surrounds. The menu includes Hanoi-style crispy duck rolls. 6-11pm Sun-Wed, to midnight Thu-Sat $$

items.name: Fiata Pizza
items.info: Shop & Dine in Central Market · For many, the southern Italian-style pizzas here are Hong Kong’s best. Perfect for a casual date night. noon-3.30pm & 6-10.30pm $$

items.name: Honky Tonks Tavern
items.info: The loyal crowd spills out the door at happy hour, for cocktails, craft beer and pizza. 5pm-midnight Mon-Thu, to 1am Fri, 3pm-1am Sat & Sun

items.name: Dead Poets HK
items.info: A barbershop by day, this is a stripped-back cocktail bar pulling in a young crowd. Drinks are themed to dead songwriters and rappers. 9am-1pm

items.name: The Diplomat
items.info: This pocket-sized diner slash cocktail bar combines classic drinks with brasserie-style bar snacks like truffled mac & cheese. 6pm-2am Mon-Sat

items.name: Dragonfly
items.info: Late Nights in Lan Kwai Fong World’s Longest Urban Escalator · Inside Tai Kwun, this cocktail lounge shimmers with an otherworldly glass design inspired by Tiffany lamps. 5pm-1am Sun-Thu, to 2am Fri & Sat

items.name: Amber
items.info: Inside the Mandarin Oriental with two Michelin stars, Amber fuses traditional French food with modern Asian flavours. noon-1.45pm & 6pm-midnight $$

items.name: Lung King Heen
items.info: The world’s first Chinese restaurant to receive three Michelin stars. noon-2.30pm & 5-9pm Mon-Fri, from 11.30am Sat & Sun $$$

items.name: Magistracy Dining Room
items.info: Old-world splendour inside one of Tai Kwun’s former courthouses. 6pm-midnight Mon-Wed, from noon Thu-Sun $$$

items.name: Bo Innovation
items.info: Central’s Marvellous Mosque · ‘Demon Chef’ Alvin Leung retools Cantonese classics with molecular gastronomy. noon-3pm & 6pm-midnight Wed-Sat, 6pm-midnight Mon & Tue $$$

items.name: Savoury Project
items.info: From the team behind Coa, this savoury cocktail concept pours umami-rich drinks like ‘Thai Beef Salad’. 6pm-1am Tue-Sat, to midnight Sun

items.name: Argo
items.info: Voted Time Out’s ‘coolest bar in the world’ in 2021, Argo in the Four Seasons combines inventive concoctions with story-telling flair. 5pm-1am Sun-Thu, to 2am Fri & Sat

items.name: Kinsman
items.info: Pays homage to Hong Kong heritage; local spirits are used to create drinks like Satsuma Snow, made with sweet rice wine. 5pm-midnight Mon-Thu, to 1am Fri & Sat

items.name: Quinary
items.info: Say You Want a Revolution · Uses homemade infusions to create Asian-inspired cocktails like its signature Earl Grey Caviar Martini. 5pm-1am Mon-Sat, to midnight Sunday

items.name: Please Don’t Tell
items.info: Duck into a phone booth at MO Bar for New York-inspired cocktails, hot dogs, burgers and loaded tater tots. 5pm-midnight

items.name: The Green Door
items.info: Hidden in an alley off Graham Street Market, this subterranean cocktail bar evokes a Roman wine cellar. 6pm-1am Sun-Wed, to 2am Thu-Sat
Ring the doorbell to be let into this Tai Kwun speakeasy (building 13). Prohibition-themed, visits limited to 90 minutes. 5pm-midnight Sun-Thu, to 1am Fri & Sat

items.name: Dr Fern’s Gin Parlour
items.info: Duck Eggs & Dragonfruit · Hidden behind a waiting room door in the Landmark mall (enter from Pedder St), Dr Fern’s has more than 300 gins. noon-1am Sun-Thu, to 2am Fri & Sat

items.name: Cardinal Point
items.info: Enjoy harbour views from the 45th-floor roof terrace of The Landmark. DJs supply the sundowner soundtrack. noon-1am Sat-Fri, to 10pm Sun

items.name: Grand Majestic Bar
items.info: Book a table on the terrace of the Grand Majestic Sichuan for cocktails infused with Chinese ingredients. 6-10pm Tue-Sun, to 10.45pm Fri & Sat

items.name: La Suite at Clarence
items.info: Inside French restaurant Clarence, this bar has an outdoor lounge with awesome skyline views. 4pm-midnight Mon-Thu, to 1am Fri & Sat

items.name: Popinjays
items.info: Let Them Eat Snake Hong Kong’s OG Milk Tea Exceptional Egg Tarts One Sauce to Rule Them All Way out West to Kennedy Town Dim Sum before Dawn · Chic bar and restaurant on the roof of the Murray hotel. Take a table on the wraparound terrace for cocktails, wine, craft beers and killer views. noon-11pm

items.name: Kau Kee
items.info: Queue up to savour the beef brisket noodle soups at this Hong Kong institution, in business since the 1930s. 12.30-10.30pm Mon-Sat $

items.name: Mammy Pancake
items.info: Mammy’s fluffy egg puffs (bubble-wrap-shaped waffles) are filled with sweet treats like matcha, banana. noon-9pm Mon-Sat, to 8pm Sun $

items.name: Sing Heung Yuen
items.info: A quintessential dai pai dong (food stall), diners squeeze around tables for macaroni in tomato soup, French toast and milk tea. 8am-3.30pm Mon-Sat $

items.name: Sheung Wan Cooked Food Centre
items.info: Temple Hopping Tai Ping Shan A History of Pandemics · Check Cantonese, Thai and other vendors before sitting down at this sprawling canteen. 6am-10pm $

items.name: Sun Hing Restaurant
items.info: Deliciously chaotic Kennedy Town stalwart that opens well before dawn for handmade dim sum. 3am-4pm $

items.name: Sky Cuisine
items.info: Classic dim sum in Sheung Wan that attracts an older local crowd. Taste and quality are both top-notch. 7am-11pm $$

items.name: Sheung Hei
items.info: Kennedy Town restaurant serving all the classic savoury and sweet dim sum with Cantonese stir-fries and claypot rice. 24hr $

items.name: Chau Kee
items.info: Antique Adventures Strolling in Sai Ying Pun Feast at a Cooked Food Centre · This cha chaan tang (tea house) serves decent dim sum in Sai Ying Pun alongside the usual French toast and milk tea. 10am-9pm Tue-Sun $

items.name: Coa
items.info: Asia’s best bar for three years running, Coa in Sheung Wan is all about the flavours of Mexico. Expect to queue. 6am-midnight Tue-Thu & Sun, to 1am Fri & Sat

items.name: Mostly Harmless
items.info: This relaxed Sai Ying Pun bar serves a daily changing menu of four cocktails that focus on local ingredients, and twisted classics. 4pm-midnight Wed-Sun

items.name: The Old Man
items.info: Creative mixology is the MO at this Sheung Wan bar themed to Hemingway. Snag a seat at the communal table inset with ice. 5pm-1am Sun-Wed, to 2am Thu-Sat

items.name: Dead Poets HK
items.info: Follow Your Nose for Dried Seafood · A Sheung Wan barbershop by day, it morphs into a bar serving cocktails dedicated to dead songwriters and rappers by night. 9am-1pm

items.name: Cafe Hunan
items.info: This casual Sai Ying Pun restaurant brings the fire with chilli-laced fish, smoky tofu and Chairman Mao’s red braised pork. 11.30am-3pm & 5.30-10pm $$

items.name: Chuen Cheung Kui
items.info: Sample the cuisine of the migratory Hakka people - hearty fare like braised stews and tofu stuffed with pork. 11am-10pm $$

items.name: Kwan Kee Claypot Rice
items.info: Rice cooked in an earthen pot and topped with meat and fish sounds simple enough but this eatery takes it to another level. 5.30-10pm $

items.name: Sang Kee Congee
items.info: One-Stop Shop for Local Artisans · A hug in a bowl, the congee (rice porridge) at this hyperlocal breakfast spot can be zhooshed up with pork, fish or preserved egg. 6.30am-8.30pm Mon-Sat $

items.name: Catch
items.info: Smashed avo, shakshuka, and steak and eggs star on the brunch menu at this Aussie-run spot in Sai Ying Pun. 11.30am-10pm Tue-Fri, from 10am Sat & Sun $$

items.name: LucAle
items.info: Italian favourites like homemade pasta and tiramisu are crafted with artisanal ingredients at this neighbourhood gem. 6-11.30pm Mon-Fri, noon-3pm Sat & Sun $$
